message.content:
Create 13 realistic text documents for testing a YAML/Markdown/Python/R formatter. Write them into /tmp/corpus11/n/ (create it). Do NOT run any formatter or other program on them; just write the files (Write tool or shell heredoc). Do not write anything outside /tmp/corpus11/.

Exact file names: ansible_playbook.yml, changelog.md, contributing.md, docker_compose.yml, github_workflow.yml, kubernetes_multi_document.yaml, mkdocs_config.yml, openapi.yaml, python_script.py, quarto_report.qmd, r_script.R, readme.md, rmarkdown_sentence_wrap.Rmd.

Theme for this batch: large, long-lived enterprise and open-source projects, maximally varied formatting habits. Make each file feel like it was edited by several people:
- Markdown files: mixtures of `*`, `-` and `+` bullets; numbered lists starting at numbers other than 1; list items containing block quotes, tables or fenced code; deeply nested lists (3-4 levels) with 2- and 4-space indentation styles; headings that skip levels; emphasis with underscores and asterisks; strikethrough `~~x~~`; inline code containing backticks (``` `` `code` `` ```); very long table rows; HTML blocks such as `<details>`/`<summary>`, `<table>`, `<!-- comments -->`; link reference definitions; images with width attributes; line breaks; keyboard keys <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>; trailing whitespace; a few lines with hard tabs inside code blocks.
- changelog.md: 8+ versions, dates in various formats, "Unreleased" section, sub-bullets, links to compare views as reference definitions at the bottom, some entries spanning multiple lines with lazy continuation (continuation lines not indented).
- YAML files: very long (aim for 150-250 lines each), with heavy commenting (including commented-out blocks of YAML), anchors & aliases with merge keys `<<: [*a, *b]`, long flow mappings on one line exceeding 120 characters, block scalars containing shell scripts and JSON, quoted strings containing `: ` and `#`, keys that need quoting, values like `"*"`, `'@scope/pkg'`, `0755`, `1e3`, `null`, and empty mappings `{}` / sequences `[]`. Kubernetes file with 6+ documents including a CustomResourceDefinition-like schema with nested `properties:` and `description:` lines. OpenAPI 3.1 with `oneOf`, `allOf`, `discriminator`, `examples`, long `description: |` Markdown blocks. All YAML must be valid (spaces only for indentation).
- python_script.py: a long CLI tool (argparse subcommands, dataclasses, typing, logging, pathlib, async), with 3 `# fmt: markdown` comment lines each directly above a target: a module-level triple-quoted Markdown string assignment (`HELP = """...`, use r""" if it contains backslashes), or a block of `#` comment lines with Markdown. Include a Markdown table and nested list in one of them.
- r_script.R: a long R script with functions, roxygen blocks, pipes `|>` and `%>%`, `data.table` syntax, and 2 `# fmt: markdown` lines each directly above a block of `#` comment lines with Markdown or above a multi-line string assignment (no backslashes in non-raw strings).
- quarto_report.qmd: Quarto report with tabsets (`::: {.panel-tabset}`), columns layout, callouts of several types, code cells with `#|` options, figures with layout options, a mermaid diagram cell, footnotes, cross-refs.
- rmarkdown_sentence_wrap.Rmd: front matter with `editor_options:` / `markdown:` / `wrap: sentence` and a `params:` block, long multi-sentence paragraphs, abbreviations (e.g., i.e., Dr., Fig.), numbered and bulleted lists, chunks, inline r.

UTF-8, LF line endings. Reply only with the list of files and their line counts.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

---
# fmt: skip file
title: Directives
description: Tell Yamark what to format, skip, preserve, or configure from inside the file.
---

<!-- fmt: skip file -->

The source file is the primary interface. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to
the text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.
Because directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.
The comment marker depends on the file:

| File | Directive comment |
| --- | --- |
| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |
| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |

Quarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.

## Target the next value or block

Most directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target
is usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal
or a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the
surrounding Python or R source code.

## YAML files

Mark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:

```yaml
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
description: "Explain the project in a few clear sentences."
other_value: "This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown."
```

The directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is
another way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:

```yaml
instructions: !markdown |
  # Review

  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.
```

Use the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the
language after `fmt:`:

```yaml
# fmt: python
script: |
  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)
```

YAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes
the collection rather than a scalar:

```yaml
# fmt: table
- {name: alpha, type: string, default: ""}
- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}
```

## Python files

Put `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block
that contains Markdown:

```python
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
REVIEW_PROMPT = """
# Review

Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.
"""
```

The `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the
marked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.

The same directive can target a Markdown comment block:

```python
# fmt: markdown
# # Filters
#
# Apply the most specific filter first.
#
# - Each filter is a single expression.
```

For a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:

```python
# fmt: r
analysis = """
f <- function(x) x + 1
"""
```

## R files

R uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a
vignette, help text, or a Shiny message:

```r
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
help_text <- r"(
# Filters

Apply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.
)"
```

It can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:

```r
# fmt: markdown
# # Filters
#
# Apply the most specific filter first.
#
# - Each filter is a single expression.
```

For source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name
in the same way as in a YAML file:

```yaml
# fmt: r
analysis: |
  f <- function(x)x+1
```

## Control a region or a whole file

The scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.
Use `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide
setting:

| Scope | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| `scope=next` | The next supported string, scalar, collection, or comment block. |
| `scope=from-here` | Supported content from this point until another directive changes the setting. |
| `scope=file` | The whole file, including supported content before the directive. |

Skip one target:

```yaml
normal: [1, 2, 3]
# fmt: skip
manual:
    -   [ 1,2,3]
```

Preserve a region and resume formatting afterward:

```markdown
<!-- fmt: off -->
#   Keep this heading ##

<!-- fmt: on -->
```

Skip a whole file by putting the file directive at the top. YAML, Python, and R
use the same hash-comment form:

```text
# fmt: skip file
```

Markdown uses an HTML comment:

```markdown
<!-- fmt: skip file -->
```

A whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is
intentionally outside Yamark's scope.

Markdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected
content, including supported nested Markdown.

## Preserve intentional table widths

Yamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored
widths while still formatting its contents:

```markdown
<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->
+----------+------------------+
| Name     | Description      |
+==========+==================+
| A        | Short text       |
+----------+------------------+
```

Use `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or

---
# =============================================================================
# site.yml -- Northwind Commerce fleet: baseline, web tier, database tier
#
# Owners:   platform-infra (primary) / sre-oncall (secondary)
# Runbook:  https://wiki.northwind.example/display/INFRA/Site+Playbook
#
# Typical runs:
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod site.yml --limit 'web:&ams1' --check --diff
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging site.yml -t baseline,deploy -e deploy_version=4.18.2
#
# History: merged from three playbooks in 2021 (INFRA-1902). YAML anchors were
# added in 2023 so nobody copy/pastes retry settings again; the YAML loader
# resolves them, Ansible only ever sees the merged result.
# =============================================================================

- name: "Baseline: every host in the inventory"
  hosts: all
  become: true
  gather_facts: true
  serial: "25%"
  max_fail_percentage: 10
  vars:
    retry_policy: &retry
      retries: 5
      delay: 10
    proxy_env: &proxy_env
      http_proxy: "http://proxy.corp.northwind.example:3128"
      https_proxy: "http://proxy.corp.northwind.example:3128"
      no_proxy: "localhost,127.0.0.1,169.254.169.254,.corp.northwind.example"
    locale_env: &locale_env
      LANG: C.UTF-8
      LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
    baseline_packages:
      - curl
      - jq
      - unzip
      - chrony
      - auditd
      - python3-pip
    # baseline_packages_legacy:        # Ubuntu 18.04 only, gone since the 2024 refresh
    #   - ntp
    #   - nagios-nrpe-server
    #   - python2.7
    # yamllint disable-line rule:line-length
    sysctl_tuning: { net.core.somaxconn: 4096, net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog: 8192, vm.swappiness: 10, fs.file-max: 2097152, net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range: "1024 65535" }
    sudoers_rules:
      "%wheel": "ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL"
      "%deploy": "ALL=(storefront) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart storefront"
      "@ops-oncall": "ALL=(ALL) ALL"
    log_retention_days: 14
    ssh_banner: "Authorized use only: activity is logged and monitored # SEC-118"
    extra_apt_repos: []
    host_overrides: {}
    legacy_agent_version: null

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refuse to run against hosts without a datacenter
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - dc is defined
          - dc in ['ams1', 'fra2', 'iad3']
        fail_msg: 'Host {{ inventory_hostname }} has no "dc" var: check inventories/*/group_vars/all.yml'
        quiet: true
      tags: [always]

  tasks:
    - name: Install baseline packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: "{{ baseline_packages }}"
        state: present
        update_cache: true
        cache_valid_time: 3600
      environment:
        <<: [*proxy_env, *locale_env]
        DEBIAN_FRONTEND: noninteractive
      register: apt_result
      until: apt_result is succeeded
      <<: *retry
      tags:
      - baseline
      - packages

    - name: Apply kernel tunables
      ansible.posix.sysctl:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
        sysctl_file: /etc/sysctl.d/90-northwind.conf
        reload: yes
      loop: "{{ sysctl_tuning | dict2items }}"
      loop_control: { label: "{{ item.key }}={{ item.value }}" }
      tags: [baseline, sysctl]

    - name: Manage sudoers drop-ins
      ansible.builtin.copy:
          dest: "/etc/sudoers.d/50-{{ item.key | regex_replace('[^A-Za-z0-9_-]', '') }}"
          content: "{{ item.key }} {{ item.value }}\n"
          mode: 0440
          validate: /usr/sbin/visudo -cf %s
      loop: "{{ sudoers_rules | dict2items }}"

    - name: Harden sshd
      ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
        path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        regexp: '^#?\s*{{ item.key }}\s'
        line: "{{ item.key }} {{ item.value }}"
        validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
      loop:
        - { key: PermitRootLogin, value: "no" }
        - { key: PasswordAuthentication, value: "no" }
        - { key: Banner, value: /etc/issue.net }
        - { key: AllowGroups, value: "ssh-users wheel" }
      notify: Restart sshd

    - name: Compress and expire application logs
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -euo pipefail
        shopt -s nullglob
        # gzip anything older than a day, delete archives past retention
        find /var/log/northwind -type f -name '*.log' -mtime +1 -print0 \
          | xargs -0 --no-run-if-empty gzip -9 --force
        find /var/log/northwind -type f -name '*.gz' -mtime +{{ log_retention_days }} -delete
        du -sh /var/log/northwind | awk '{print "log dir size: " $1}'
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      changed_when: false
      tags: [logs]

    #TODO(jkowalski): drop once the last CentOS 7 box is gone (INFRA-3120)
    # - name: Install legacy monitoring agent
    #   ansible.builtin.yum:
    #     name: "https://repo.northwind.example/agent/agent-{{ legacy_agent_version }}.x86_64.rpm"
    #   when: legacy_agent_version is not none

  handlers:
    - name: Restart sshd
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: ssh
        state: restarted


- name: Web tier (nginx + node storefront)
  hosts: "web:&{{ target_dc | default('ams1') }}"
  become: yes
  serial: [1, "30%", "100%"]
  vars:
    app_user: storefront
    app_root: /srv/storefront
    deploy_version: "4.18.2"
    env_name: "{{ 'production' if 'prod' in inventory_dir else 'staging' }}"
    npm_globals:
      - pm2@5.3.1
      - '@northwind/storefront-cli'
      - '@scope/pkg'
      - "@northwind/feature-flags@^2.1.0"
    nginx_upstreams:
      "storefront:3000": { weight: 5, max_fails: 3, fail_timeout: 10s }
      "storefront-canary:3001": { weight: 1, max_fails: 1, fail_timeout: 5s }
    cors_allowed_origins: "*"
    nginx_extra_locations: []

  tasks:
    - name: Install global npm packages
      community.general.npm:
        name: "{{ item }}"
        global: true
        state: present
      loop: "{{ npm_globals }}"
      environment: *proxy_env

    - name: Deploy storefront release
      tags: [deploy]
      block:
        - name: Create release directory
          ansible.builtin.file:
            path: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ deploy_version }}"
            state: directory
            owner: "{{ app_user }}"
            mode: 0755

        - name: Fetch release tarball
          ansible.builtin.get_url:
            url: "https://artifacts.northwind.example/storefront/{{ deploy_version }}/storefront.tgz"
            dest: "/tmp/storefront-{{ deploy_version }}.tgz"
            checksum: "sha256:https://artifacts.northwind.example/storefront/{{ deploy_version }}/SHA256SUMS"
            headers: { Authorization: "Bearer {{ artifact_token }}", Accept: application/octet-stream, X-Requested-By: ansible }
          environment: *proxy_env
          register: fetch
          until: fetch is succeeded
          <<: *retry

        - name: Write runtime config (JSON)
          ansible.builtin.copy:
            dest: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ deploy_version }}/config/runtime.json"
            owner: "{{ app_user }}"
            mode: "0640"
            content: |
              {
                "env": "{{ env_name }}",
                "port": 3000,
                "cors": { "origins": ["{{ cors_allowed_origins }}"], "credentials": false },
                "featureFlags": { "provider": "@northwind/feature-flags", "pollIntervalMs": 30000 },
                "logLevel": "info"
              }

        - name: Switch the current symlink and reload pm2
          ansible.builtin.shell: |
            set -e
            ln -sfn "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ deploy_version }}" "{{ app_root }}/current"
            sudo -u {{ app_user }} pm2 reload ecosystem.config.js --update-env
            for i in $(seq 1 30); do
              curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/healthz && exit 0
              sleep 2
            done
            echo "storefront failed its health check after 60s" >&2
            exit 1
          args:
            chdir: "{{ app_root }}/current"
      rescue:
        - name: Roll back to the previous release
          ansible.builtin.command: "{{ app_root }}/bin/rollback --to previous --reason 'deploy #{{ deploy_version }} failed: health check'"
        - ansible.builtin.fail:
            msg: "Deployment of {{ deploy_version }} was rolled back on {{ inventory_hostname }}"
      always:
        - name: Remove downloaded tarball
          ansible.builtin.file:
            path: "/tmp/storefront-{{ deploy_version }}.tgz"
            state: absent

  handlers:
    - name: Reload nginx
      ansible.builtin.service: { name: nginx, state: reloaded }


- name: Database tier (PostgreSQL primaries)
  hosts: db_primary
  become: true
  gather_facts: true
  vars:
      pg_version: 16
      pg_hba_entries:
          - { type: hostssl, database: storefront, user: storefront, address: "10.20.0.0/16", method: scram-sha-256 }
          - { type: hostssl, database: replication, user: replicator, address: "10.20.8.0/24", method: scram-sha-256, comment: "replicas: fra2 + iad3" }
          - { type: local, database: all, user: postgres, method: peer }
      pg_settings:
          shared_buffers: 8GB
          work_mem: 32MB
          max_connections: 400
          "auto_explain.log_min_duration": 1e3
          log_line_prefix: '%m [%p] %q%u@%d '
          archive_command: "test ! -f /mnt/wal/%f && cp %p /mnt/wal/%f"

  tasks:
    - name: Configure pg_hba.conf
      community.postgresql.postgresql_pg_hba:
        dest: "/etc/postgresql/{{ pg_version }}/main/pg_hba.conf"
        contype: "{{ item.type }}"
        databases: "{{ item.database }}"
        users: "{{ item.user }}"
        source: "{{ item.address | default(omit) }}"
        method: "{{ item.method }}"
        create: true
      loop: "{{ pg_hba_entries }}"
      notify: Reload postgresql

    - name: Apply postgresql.conf settings
      community.postgresql.postgresql_set:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
      loop: "{{ pg_settings | dict2items }}"
      become_user: postgres
      notify: Restart postgresql   # shared_buffers needs a restart; a reload is not enough

    - name: Take a base backup before schema migrations
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: "pg_basebackup -D /mnt/backup/pre-migrate-{{ ansible_date_time.iso8601_basic_short }} -Ft -z -P"
      become_user: postgres
      run_once: true
      when: run_migrations | default(false) | bool and not ansible_check_mode

    # - name: Enable pg_stat_statements (moved into the postgres role, 2024.2)
    #   community.postgresql.postgresql_ext:
    #     name: pg_stat_statements
    #     db: storefront
    #   become_user: postgres

  handlers:
    - name: Reload postgresql
      ansible.builtin.service: { name: "postgresql@{{ pg_version }}-main", state: reloaded }
    - name: Restart postgresql
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: "postgresql@{{ pg_version }}-main"
        state: restarted
      throttle: 1


- name: Announce the rollout
  hosts: localhost
  connection: local
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: Post a summary to Slack
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: "{{ slack_webhook_url }}"
        method: POST
        body_format: json
        body:
          channel: "#releases"
          username: ansible-bot
          text: "Storefront {{ hostvars[groups['web'][0]].deploy_version | default('n/a') }} rolled out: OK"
          attachments: []
        status_code: [200, 204]
      when: slack_webhook_url | default('') | length > 0
      ignore_errors: true
...

# docker-compose.yml -- local development stack for Helios (self-hosted product analytics)
#
#   cp .env.example .env && docker compose up -d --wait
#   docker compose --profile observability --profile workers up -d
#   docker compose config --quiet            # validate after editing this file!
#
# House rules (reviewers WILL ask):
#   * shared settings live in the x-* blocks below and are merged with `<<`
#   * ports are always quoted ("8080:80"): YAML 1.1 reads 22:22 as a base-60 int
#   * use $$ for a literal dollar sign inside container shell snippets
#
# Spec: https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/
name: helios

x-port-registry:   # documentation only -- compose ignores x-* keys
  "8000": api (gunicorn)
  "5173": frontend (vite dev server)
  "9000": "minio: S3 API"
  "9001": "minio: web console"
  "3000": grafana

x-logging: &default-logging
  logging: { driver: "json-file", options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "5", tag: "{{.Name}}/{{.ImageName}}", labels: "dev.helios.service" } }

x-restart: &default-restart
  restart: unless-stopped

x-healthcheck: &healthcheck-defaults
  interval: 10s
  timeout: 5s
  retries: 10
  start_period: 20s

x-app-env: &app-env
  HELIOS_ENV: development
  DATABASE_URL: "postgres://helios:helios@postgres:5432/helios?sslmode=disable"
  REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
  S3_ENDPOINT: http://minio:9000
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://tempo:4317
  OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG: "0.25"
  HELIOS_INGEST_FLUSH_MS: 1e3
  LOG_FORMAT: json
  # LOG_LEVEL: debug        # handy locally -- never commit it uncommented
  CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "*"
  FEATURE_FLAGS: '{"newIngestPipeline": true, "betaDashboards": false, "sampling": {"rate": 0.1}}'

x-app-base: &app-base
  image: ghcr.io/helios-oss/helios:${HELIOS_TAG:-edge}
  build:
    context: .
    dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile
    args:
      PYTHON_VERSION: "3.12"
      NODE_VERSION: "20"
      NPM_SCOPE: '@helios'
    cache_from: [ "ghcr.io/helios-oss/helios:buildcache" ]
  env_file: [.env]
  depends_on:
    postgres: { condition: service_healthy }
    redis: { condition: service_healthy }
  networks: [backend]

services:
  api:
    <<: [*app-base, *default-logging, *default-restart]
    command: ["gunicorn", "helios.wsgi:application", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000", "--workers", "4", "--access-logfile", "-"]
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      HELIOS_ROLE: api
      GUNICORN_CMD_ARGS: "--timeout 120 --graceful-timeout 30"
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
      - "127.0.0.1:5678:5678"   # debugpy, bound to localhost only
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/healthz || exit 1"]
    labels:
      dev.helios.service: api
      dev.helios.team: "core-platform"
      traefik.http.routers.api.rule: "Host(`api.helios.localhost`) && PathPrefix(`/v1`)"
      traefik.http.services.api.loadbalancer.server.port: "8000"

  worker:
    <<: [*app-base, *default-logging, *default-restart]
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
    command:
      - |
        set -eu
        echo "waiting for migrations..."
        until python -m helios.manage migrate --check > /dev/null 2>&1; do
          sleep 3
        done
        exec celery -A helios.tasks worker \
          --loglevel="$${CELERY_LOG_LEVEL:-info}" \
          --concurrency="$${CELERY_CONCURRENCY:-4}" \
          -Q default,ingest,exports
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      HELIOS_ROLE: worker
      C_FORCE_ROOT: "false"
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
      resources:
        limits: { cpus: "1.50", memory: 1G }
        reservations: { cpus: "0.25", memory: 256M }
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: ["CMD", "celery", "-A", "helios.tasks", "inspect", "ping", "-d", "celery@$$HOSTNAME"]
    configs:
      - source: worker_entrypoint
        target: /usr/local/bin/helios-entrypoint
        mode: 0755

  scheduler:
    <<: [*app-base, *default-logging]
    command: celery -A helios.tasks beat --schedule /tmp/celerybeat-schedule --pidfile=
    restart: on-failure:3
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      HELIOS_ROLE: scheduler
    profiles: ["workers"]

  frontend:
    image: node:20-alpine
    working_dir: /app
    command: sh -c 'corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --filter "$$PNPM_FILTER" dev --host 0.0.0.0'
    volumes:
      - ./web:/app:cached
      - frontend_node_modules:/app/node_modules
    ports: ["5173:5173"]
    environment:
      PNPM_FILTER: '@helios/web'
      VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:8000
      CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING: "true"
    <<: *default-logging

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16.4-bookworm
    <<: [*default-logging, *default-restart]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: helios
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: helios      # local only; staging/prod read it from Vault
      POSTGRES_DB: helios
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C.UTF-8 --data-checksums"
    command: >
      postgres
        -c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements
        -c log_min_duration_statement=250
        -c max_connections=200
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./docker/postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
    shm_size: 256mb
    networks: [backend]

  redis:
    image: redis:7.2-alpine
    <<: [*default-logging, *default-restart]
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--maxmemory", "512mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
    sysctls:
      net.core.somaxconn: 1024
    ulimits:
      nofile: { soft: 65536, hard: 65536 }
    networks: [backend]

  minio:
    image: quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-08-17T01-24-54Z
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: helios
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: helios-dev-secret
    ports: ["9000:9000", "9001:9001"]
    volumes: ["minio:/data"]
    profiles: [storage]
    networks: [backend]

  nginx:
    image: nginx:1.27-alpine
    depends_on: [api, frontend]
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    configs:
      - source: nginx_conf
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
        mode: 0440
    secrets:
      - source: tls_cert
        target: /etc/nginx/tls/helios.crt
      - source: tls_key
        target: /etc/nginx/tls/helios.key
        mode: 0400
    <<: [*default-logging, *default-restart]
    networks: [backend, edge]

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.54.1
    profiles: [observability]
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=7d
      - --web.enable-lifecycle
    configs:
      - source: prometheus_yml
        target: /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
    ports: ["9090:9090"]
    networks: [backend]

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana-oss:11.2.0
    profiles: [observability]
    environment:
      GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED: "true"
      GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ORG_ROLE: Admin
      GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS: "grafana-clock-panel,grafana-piechart-panel"
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: null       # inherit from the host shell if set
    configs:
      - source: grafana_datasources
        target: /etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources/helios.json
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
    volumes: [grafana:/var/lib/grafana]
    depends_on: [prometheus]

# .github/workflows/ci.yml -- main pipeline for the Lumen monorepo
#
#   sdk/python  -> ruff, pytest matrix, integration tests against real services
#   packages/*  -> eslint + vitest per workspace package
#   crates/*    -> clippy + cargo test on stable and on the MSRV
#
# Job names are referenced by branch protection and the merge queue: talk to
# release-eng (#ci-help) before renaming anything.
# yamllint disable rule:line-length rule:truthy
name: "CI: build, test & release"

"on":
  push:
    branches: [main, "release/**"]
    tags: ["v*.*.*", "sdk-v*"]
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"
      - .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  merge_group: {}
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 3 * * 1-5"   # weekday nightly, deliberately off the hour
    - cron: '0 12 * * 0'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run-benchmarks:
        description: "Run benchmarks: slow (~40 min)"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      publish-target:
        description: 'Registry to publish to # leave empty for a dry run'
        type: choice
        options: ["", npm, pypi, crates, all]
        default: ""
      log-level:
        description: RUST_LOG / LOG_LEVEL override
        required: false
        default: null

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK: "1"
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"
  NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=6144
  VITEST_HOOK_TIMEOUT: 1e3
  DEFAULT_UMASK: 0022
  LOG_LEVEL: ${{ inputs.log-level || 'info' }}

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Detect changed areas
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      python: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.python }}
      node: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.node }}
      rust: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.rust }}
    steps:
      - &checkout
        name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            python:
              - 'sdk/python/**'
              - 'pyproject.toml'
            node:
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
            rust:
              - 'crates/**'
              - 'Cargo.lock'

  lint:
    name: "Lint: ruff, eslint, clippy"
    needs: changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions: { contents: read }
    env: &lint-env
      RUFF_OUTPUT_FORMAT: github
      ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG: "true"
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: &node-with
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: ESLint
        run: pnpm -r --filter "./packages/*" lint -- --max-warnings=0
      - name: Ruff
        uses: astral-sh/ruff-action@v3
        with: { src: sdk/python, args: "check --output-format=github" }
      - name: Clippy
        if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

  test-python:
    name: "Python ${{ matrix.python }} / ${{ matrix.os }}"
    needs: [changes, lint]
    if: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.python == 'true' || github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 6
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-14, windows-2022]
        python: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        experimental: [false]
        exclude:
          - { os: macos-14, python: "3.10" }
          - { os: windows-2022, python: "3.11" }
        include:
          - { os: ubuntu-24.04, python: "3.14-dev", experimental: true, label: "nightly CPython", pip-cache: ~/.cache/pip }
          - { os: windows-2022, python: "3.12", experimental: false, label: "Windows / py3.12", pip-cache: '~\AppData\Local\pip\Cache' }
    env:
      <<: *lint-env
      COVERAGE_FILE: .coverage.${{ matrix.os }}.${{ matrix.python }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: sdk/python
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
          allow-prereleases: true
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: "sdk/python/requirements/*.txt"
      - name: Install
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel
          python -m pip install -e ".[test]" -c requirements/constraints.txt
      - name: Unit tests
        run: |
          pytest -q -n auto --cov=lumen --cov-report=xml \
            --junitxml="reports/junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python }}.xml" \
            -m "not integration and not slow"
      # - name: Upload coverage to Codecov (disabled: token rotation, see #4471)
      #   uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
      #   with:
      #     files: sdk/python/coverage.xml
      #     flags: python-${{ matrix.python }}

  integration:
    name: Integration (postgres + redis)
    needs: test-python
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions: { contents: read }
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env: &db-env
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: lumen_test
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U postgres"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 20
      redis:
        image: redis:7
        ports: ["6379:6379"]
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.12", cache: pip, cache-dependency-path: "sdk/python/requirements/*.txt" }
      - name: Run integration suite
        env:
          <<: [*lint-env, *db-env]
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/lumen_test
          REDIS_URL: "redis://localhost:6379/0"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python -m pip install -e "sdk/python[test,postgres]"
          pytest sdk/python/tests/integration \
            --junitxml=reports/junit-integration.xml \
            -m "integration and not slow" -p no:cacheprovider
          echo "### Integration summary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          python scripts/ci/summarize_junit.py reports/junit-integration.xml >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  test-node:
    name: "Node ${{ matrix.node }}: ${{ matrix.package }}"
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.node == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions: { contents: read }
    strategy:
      matrix:
        package: ['@lumen/core', '@lumen/react', "@lumen/cli", '@scope/pkg']
        node: [18, 20, 22]
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          <<: *node-with
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter "${{ matrix.package }}" test -- --coverage --reporter=junit --outputFile=reports/junit.xml

  rust:
    name: "Rust (${{ matrix.toolchain }}, ${{ matrix.os }})"
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    permissions: { contents: read }
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-14]
        toolchain: [stable, "1.79"]   # 1.79 == MSRV, bump together with Cargo.toml
    env:
      SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED: "true"
      RUSTC_WRAPPER: sccache
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with: { toolchain: "${{ matrix.toolchain }}", components: "clippy, rustfmt" }
      - uses: mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.6
      - run: cargo test --workspace --locked --all-features
      - name: Benchmarks (manual runs only)
        if: inputs.run-benchmarks && matrix.toolchain == 'stable' && runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: cargo bench -p lumen-core -- --output-format bencher | tee bench.txt

  release:
    name: Publish packages
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || inputs.publish-target != ''
    needs: [integration, test-node, rust]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment:
      name: release
      url: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/tag/${{ github.ref_name }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write      # trusted publishing (PyPI) + npm provenance
      attestations: write
    env:
      BIN_MODE: 0755
      PUBLISH_TARGET: ${{ inputs.publish-target || 'all' }}
    steps:
      - <<: *checkout
        with: { fetch-depth: 1, persist-credentials: false }
      - name: Build artifacts
        run: |
          make dist
          find dist -type f -name 'lumen-*' -exec install -m "$BIN_MODE" {} dist/bin/ \;
          ls -la dist/
      - name: Write release metadata
        run: |
          cat > dist/release.json <<'JSON'
          {
            "version": "${{ github.ref_name }}",
            "commit": "${{ github.sha }}",
            "packages": ["@lumen/core", "@lumen/react", "lumen-sdk", "lumen-core"],
            "channels": { "npm": "latest", "pypi": "stable" }
          }
          JSON
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            dist/*.whl
            dist/*.tar.gz
            dist/release.json
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Notify Slack
        if: always()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.27.0
        with:
          channel-id: "C0123ABCD"
          payload: |
            {
              "text": "Release ${{ github.ref_name }}: ${{ job.status }}",
              "blocks": [
                { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*${{ github.ref_name }}* finished with `${{ job.status }}` <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|logs>" } }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}

# ledger: rendered manifests for namespace fin-ledger
#
# Source of truth is deploy/helm/ledger (chart 3.9.1). This file is committed so
# Argo CD diffs stay reviewable, and for whoever still runs `kubectl apply -f`:
#   kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=platform -f kubernetes_multi_document.yaml
# YAML anchors are scoped to one document -- never alias across a `---`.
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: fin-ledger
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
    istio-injection: enabled
    "finance.example.com/cost-center": "CC-4410"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: { name: ledger-config, namespace: fin-ledger, labels: { app.kubernetes.io/name: ledger, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: finance-core } }
data:
  LOG_LEVEL: info
  HTTP_PORT: "8080"
  ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "*"
  PLUGIN_PACKAGES: '@finance/ledger-plugins'
  appsettings.json: |
    {
      "Ledger": {
        "PostingBatchSize": 500,
        "Currencies": ["EUR", "USD", "GBP", "CHF"],
        "Rounding": { "Mode": "HalfEven", "Scale": 4 }
      },
      "ConnectionStrings": { "Ledger": "Host=pg-ledger-rw.fin-ledger.svc;Database=ledger;Username=ledger" }
    }
  wait-for-db.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    # Blocks until the primary accepts connections (max ~2 minutes).
    set -eu
    i=0
    until pg_isready -h "${DB_HOST:-pg-ledger-rw}" -p 5432 -q; do
      i=$((i + 1))
      if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then echo "database not ready: giving up" >&2; exit 1; fi
      sleep 2
    done
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ledger-api
  namespace: fin-ledger
  labels: &common_labels
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: finance-core
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: helm
    helm.sh/chart: ledger-3.9.1
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"
    kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration: null
  creationTimestamp: null
spec:
  replicas: 3
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: { maxSurge: 25%, maxUnavailable: 0 }
  selector:
    matchLabels: &selector_labels
      app.kubernetes.io/name: ledger
      app.kubernetes.io/component: api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        <<: [*common_labels, *selector_labels]
        version: "3.9.1"
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "9090"
        checksum/config: 6f1c0e9b2f8d4a3c7e5b1a0d9c8b7a6f5e4d3c2b1a0f9e8d7c6b5a4f3e2d1c0b
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: ledger
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        fsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
      imagePullSecrets: []
      tolerations: []
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
        labelSelector: { matchLabels: *selector_labels }
      initContainers:
      - name: wait-for-db
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        command: ["/bin/sh", "/scripts/wait-for-db.sh"]
        volumeMounts: [{ name: scripts, mountPath: /scripts, readOnly: true }]
        securityContext: &container_security
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: "registry.example.com/finance/ledger-api:3.9.1@sha256:9b2c4f0e1d7a6b5c3e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d"
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        args: ["--config=/etc/ledger/appsettings.json", "--http-port=$(HTTP_PORT)"]
        ports:
        - { name: http, containerPort: 8080, protocol: TCP }
        - { name: metrics, containerPort: 9090 }
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef: { name: ledger-config }
        env:
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef: { name: pg-ledger-app, key: password }
        - name: POD_NAME
          valueFrom: { fieldRef: { fieldPath: metadata.name } }
        resources: &api_resources
          requests: { cpu: 250m, memory: 384Mi }
          limits: { cpu: "2", memory: 1Gi }
        livenessProbe: &http_probe
          httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: http }
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 2
          failureThreshold: 3
        readinessProbe:
          <<: *http_probe
          httpGet: { path: "/readyz?verbose=false", port: http }
          failureThreshold: 1
        startupProbe:
          <<: *http_probe
          failureThreshold: 30
        securityContext: *container_security
        volumeMounts:
        - { name: config, mountPath: /etc/ledger, readOnly: true }
        - { name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp }
      - name: otel-agent
        image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.108.0
        args: ["--config=env:OTEL_CONFIG"]
        resources:
          <<: *api_resources
          limits: { cpu: 500m, memory: 256Mi }
        securityContext:
          <<: *container_security
          runAsUser: 10002
      volumes:
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: ledger-config
          items: [{ key: appsettings.json, path: appsettings.json }]
      - name: scripts
        configMap: { name: ledger-config, defaultMode: 0755, items: [{ key: wait-for-db.sh, path: wait-for-db.sh }] }
      - name: tmp
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: ledger-api
  namespace: fin-ledger
  annotations: { service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal: "true", external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: ledger.internal.example.com. }
spec:
  selector: { app.kubernetes.io/name: ledger, app.kubernetes.io/component: api }
  ports:
    - { name: http, port: 80, targetPort: http }
    - { name: metrics, port: 9090, targetPort: metrics, appProtocol: http }
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: { name: ledger-api, namespace: fin-ledger }
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: ledger-api }
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 24
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70 }
    - type: Pods
      pods:
        metric: { name: ledger_http_requests_per_second }
        target: { type: AverageValue, averageValue: 1e3 }
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
      policies: [{ type: Percent, value: 20, periodSeconds: 60 }]
    scaleUp: {}
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: postingrules.ledger.finance.example.com
  annotations:
    controller-gen.kubebuilder.io/version: v0.16.1
spec:
  group: ledger.finance.example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    kind: PostingRule
    listKind: PostingRuleList
    plural: postingrules
    singular: postingrule
    shortNames: [prule]
  versions:
    - name: v1beta1
      served: true
      storage: true
      subresources:
        status: {}
      additionalPrinterColumns:
        - { name: Account, type: string, jsonPath: .spec.account }
        - { name: Ready, type: string, jsonPath: '.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status' }
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          description: PostingRule maps an incoming business event to one or more balanced ledger postings.
          required: [spec]
          properties:
            apiVersion:
              type: string
              description: 'APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object. Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and may reject unrecognized values.'
            kind:
              type: string
              description: "Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents: CamelCase, singular."
            metadata:
              type: object
            spec:
              type: object
              description: |
                Desired behaviour of the rule.

                Rules are evaluated in ascending `priority`; the first match wins.
                Amounts are minor units (cents), never floats.
              required: [account, match, legs]
              properties:
                account:
                  type: string
                  description: Ledger account code, e.g. "4000-REVENUE".
                  pattern: '^[0-9]{4}-[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$'
                priority:
                  type: integer
                  description: Lower runs first.
                  default: 100
                  minimum: 0
                match:
                  type: object
                  description: Event selector.
                  properties:
                    eventType:
                      type: string
                      description: CloudEvents `type` attribute; glob patterns such as "payments.*" are allowed.
                    source:
                      type: string
                      description: Optional CloudEvents source. "*" matches any source.
                      default: "*"
                    attributes:
                      type: object
                      additionalProperties: { type: string }
                legs:
                  type: array
                  description: Debit/credit legs; must sum to zero per currency.
                  minItems: 2
                  items:
                    type: object
                    required: [direction, account, amountExpr]
                    properties:
                      direction: { type: string, enum: [debit, credit], description: "Side of the posting: debit or credit." }
                      account: { type: string, description: Target account code. }
                      amountExpr:
                        type: string
                        description: >-
                          CEL expression evaluated against the event payload;
                          must return an int (minor units).
                      metadata:
                        type: object
                        x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
            status:
              type: object
              description: Observed state, written by the ledger-operator.
              properties:
                observedGeneration: { type: integer, format: int64 }
                conditions:
                  type: array
                  x-kubernetes-list-type: map
                  x-kubernetes-list-map-keys: [type]
                  items:
                    type: object
                    required: [type, status]
                    properties:
                      type: { type: string, description: "Condition type, e.g. Ready." }
                      status: { type: string, enum: ["True", "False", Unknown] }
                      message: { type: string }
                      lastTransitionTime: { type: string, format: date-time }
---
apiVersion: ledger.finance.example.com/v1beta1
kind: PostingRule
metadata:
  name: card-capture-revenue
  namespace: fin-ledger
  labels: { app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: finance-config, ledger.finance.example.com/tier: "1" }
spec:
  account: 4000-REVENUE
  priority: 10
  match:
    eventType: payments.card.captured
    source: "*"
    attributes: {}
  legs:
    - { direction: debit, account: 1100-CASH_CLEARING, amountExpr: "event.data.amount_minor" }
    - direction: credit
      account: 4000-REVENUE
      amountExpr: "event.data.amount_minor - event.data.fee_minor"
      metadata: { note: "net of PSP fees: see FIN-2207", "x-origin": legacy-import }
    - direction: credit
      account: 6100-PSP_FEES
      amountExpr: event.data.fee_minor

openapi: 3.1.0
# Public contract for the Tessera Billing API.
# Edited by hand AND by `make openapi-sync` (which only rewrites components/schemas),
# so keep long-form notes in the description blocks rather than in comments.
#
#   npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.yaml
#   npx @redocly/cli preview-docs openapi.yaml --port 8089
info:
  title: Tessera Billing API
  version: "2024-11-01"
  summary: Invoices, subscriptions and usage-based billing.
  description: |
    # Introduction

    The Tessera Billing API is organised around **REST**. It has predictable,
    resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON request bodies, returns JSON responses and uses standard HTTP verbs and status codes.

    ## Versioning
    * The API version is a date, sent in the `Tessera-Version` header.
    * Breaking changes always ship behind a new date; additive changes do not:
      - new optional request fields
      - new response fields
          + new enum values -- your client **must** tolerate unknown values

    | Header | Required | Example | Notes |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `Authorization` | yes | `Bearer tsk_live_…` | Secret keys never belong in browsers or mobile apps |
    | `Tessera-Version` | no | `2024-11-01` | Defaults to the version pinned on your account |
    | `Idempotency-Key` | POST only | `9f1c2e…` | Keys expire after 24 hours |

    ```bash
    curl https://api.tessera.example/v2/invoices \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $TESSERA_KEY" -H "Tessera-Version: 2024-11-01"
    ```

    > **Note:** amounts are integers in the currency's minor unit (cents for `usd`).
  termsOfService: https://tessera.example/legal/terms
  contact: { name: Tessera Developer Relations, url: "https://tessera.example/support", email: api@tessera.example }
  license: { name: Apache 2.0, identifier: Apache-2.0 }
  x-sdk-packages: { npm: '@tessera/billing', pypi: tessera-billing, go: "github.com/tessera/billing-go" }

servers:
  - url: https://api.tessera.example/v2
    description: Production
  - url: "https://{region}.sandbox.tessera.example/v2"
    description: Sandbox (data reset every Sunday 00:00 UTC)
    variables:
      region:
        default: eu
        enum: [eu, us, ap]
        description: "Data residency region: use the one your account lives in."

security:
  - bearerAuth: []
  - oauth2: ["billing:read"]

tags:
  - name: Invoices
    description: Create, finalize and pay invoices.
  - name: Status
    description: |
      Unauthenticated health endpoint. Safe to poll every few seconds;
      responses are cached at the edge for **5 s**.
  - name: Webhooks
    x-displayName: "Webhooks & events"

x-response-sets:   # merged into operations below with `<<`
  auth-errors: &auth_errors
    "401": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized" }
    "403": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden" }
  common-errors: &common_errors
    "429": { $ref: "#/components/responses/RateLimited" }
    5XX: { $ref: "#/components/responses/ServerError" }

paths:
  /status:
    get:
      operationId: getStatus
      tags: [Status]
      security:
        - {}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Service is up.
          headers:
            Access-Control-Allow-Origin:
              schema: { type: string, examples: ["*"] }
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  status: { type: string, enum: [ok, degraded] }
                  incident_url: { type: [string, "null"], format: uri, default: null }
  /invoices:
    get:
      operationId: listInvoices
      summary: List invoices
      tags: [Invoices]
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/StartingAfter'
        - name: status
          in: query
          description: Filter by status. Repeat the parameter to match several, e.g. `?status=open&status=draft`.
          schema:
            type: array
            items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InvoiceStatus" }
          style: form
          explode: true
      responses:
        <<: [*auth_errors, *common_errors]
        "200":
          description: A page of invoices, newest first.
          headers:
            X-RateLimit-Remaining: { description: Requests left in the current window., schema: { type: integer } }
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [data, has_more]
                properties:
                  data: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Invoice" } }
                  has_more: { type: boolean }
                  next_cursor: { type: [string, "null"] }
    post:
      operationId: createInvoice
      summary: Create an invoice
      tags: [Invoices]
      description: |
        Creates a **draft** invoice. Lines can be passed inline or added later with
        [`POST /invoices/{id}/lines`](#tag/Invoices/operation/addInvoiceLine).

        1. Draft invoices can be edited freely.
        2. Finalizing assigns a number (`INV-2024-000123`) and locks the lines.
        3. Paid invoices are immutable -- issue a credit note instead.
      parameters:
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          schema: { type: string, maxLength: 255 }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InvoiceCreate" }
            examples:
              one-off:
                summary: One-off invoice with a flat line
                value: { customer: cus_Q2w3E4r5T6y7U8, currency: eur, collection_method: send_invoice, days_until_due: 30, lines: [{ kind: flat, description: "Onboarding workshop #1", amount: 150000 }] }
              metered:
                summary: Usage line priced from a meter
                value:
                  customer: cus_Q2w3E4r5T6y7U8
                  currency: usd
                  lines:
                    - kind: usage
                      meter: api_requests
                      quantity: 1e3
                      unit_amount_decimal: "0.0425"
      responses:
        <<: *auth_errors
        "201":
          description: The created draft invoice.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Invoice" }
        "409":
          description: "Idempotency conflict: the key was already used with a different body."
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }

webhooks:
  invoice.finalized:
    post:
      summary: Invoice finalized
      description: Sent once per invoice. Delivery is *at least once*; deduplicate on `id`.
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              allOf:
                - $ref: "#/components/schemas/EventEnvelope"
                - type: object
                  properties:
                    type: { const: invoice.finalized }
                    data: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Invoice" }
      responses:
        "2XX": { description: Acknowledge within 10 seconds or the delivery is retried. }

components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: "tsk_(live|test)_*"
    oauth2:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://auth.tessera.example/oauth/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://auth.tessera.example/oauth/token
          scopes:
            "billing:read": Read invoices, subscriptions and usage
            "billing:write": Create and modify billing objects
            "webhooks:manage": "Manage webhook endpoints (admin only: requires 2FA)"
  parameters:
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 25 }
    StartingAfter:
      name: starting_after
      in: query
      description: Cursor taken from `next_cursor` of the previous page.
      schema: { type: string }
  responses:
    Unauthorized: &problem_response
      description: Missing or invalid credentials.
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
    Forbidden:
      <<: *problem_response
      description: The key is valid but lacks the required scope.
    RateLimited:
      <<: *problem_response
      description: "Too many requests: back off using the `Retry-After` header."
    ServerError:
      <<: *problem_response
      description: Something went wrong on our side. Idempotent requests are safe to retry.
  schemas:
    InvoiceStatus:
      type: string
      enum: [draft, open, paid, void, uncollectible]
    Money:
      type: object
      required: [amount, currency]
      properties:
        amount: { type: integer, description: Minor units. }
        currency: { type: string, pattern: "^[a-z]{3}$", examples: [eur, usd] }
    Invoice:
      allOf:
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Timestamps"
        - type: object
          required: [id, status, customer, total]
          properties:
            id: { type: string, readOnly: true, examples: [in_1PqRsTuVwXyZ01] }
            number: { type: [string, "null"], examples: ["INV-2024-000123", null] }
            status: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InvoiceStatus" }
            customer: { type: string }
            total: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Money" }
            lines: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InvoiceLine" } }
            metadata:
              type: object
              additionalProperties: { type: string, maxLength: 500 }
              default: {}
      examples:
        - { id: in_1PqRsTuVwXyZ01, number: null, status: draft, customer: cus_Q2w3E4r5T6y7U8, total: { amount: 150000, currency: eur }, created_at: "2024-11-04T09:30:00Z" }
    InvoiceCreate:
      type: object
      required: [customer, currency]
      properties:
        customer: { type: string }
        currency: { type: string }
        collection_method: { type: string, enum: [charge_automatically, send_invoice], default: charge_automatically }
        days_until_due: { type: integer, minimum: 0, description: "Required when `collection_method: send_invoice`." }
        lines: { type: array, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/InvoiceLine" }, maxItems: 250 }
    InvoiceLine:
      description: |
        A line is either a **flat** amount or a **usage** charge. The `kind`
        property selects the variant:

        | kind | priced by | example |
        |------|-----------|---------|
        | `flat` | `amount` | setup fee |
        | `usage` | `meter` x `unit_amount_decimal` | API calls |
      oneOf:
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/FlatLine"
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/UsageLine"
      discriminator:
        propertyName: kind
        mapping:
          flat: "#/components/schemas/FlatLine"
          usage: "#/components/schemas/UsageLine"
    FlatLine:
      type: object
      required: [kind, amount]
      properties:
        kind: { const: flat }
        description: { type: string, maxLength: 500 }
        amount: { type: integer }
    UsageLine:
      type: object
      required: [kind, meter, quantity]
      properties:
        kind: { const: usage }
        meter: { type: string, description: "Meter slug, e.g. `api_requests`." }
        quantity: { type: number, minimum: 0 }
        unit_amount_decimal: { type: string, pattern: '^\d+(\.\d{1,12})?$' }
    Timestamps:
      type: object
      properties:
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time, readOnly: true }
        updated_at: { type: [string, "null"], format: date-time, readOnly: true }
    EventEnvelope:
      type: object
      required: [id, type, created_at]
      properties:
        id: { type: string, examples: [evt_1QxYz8AbCdEf] }
        type: { type: string }
        created_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        livemode: { type: boolean }
    Problem:
      type: object
      description: RFC 9457 problem details.
      properties:
        type: { type: string, format: uri, default: "about:blank" }
        title: { type: string }
        status: { type: integer }
        detail: { type: string }
        errors:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              pointer: { type: string, examples: ["#/lines/0/amount"] }
              message: { type: string }
